name: The nine forms of devotion (navadhā bhakti)
method_summary: Devotion practised as hearing, singing and remembering the Lord's names and deeds, serving his feet, ritual worship, obeisance, servitude, friendship and complete self-offering, performed directly toward the Lord (BhP 7.5.23-24); the Śiva Purāṇa gives Śaivas the three means of hearing, singing and reflection.
signs_of_progress: melting of the heart, tears, laughter, song and dance (BhP 11.14.24; 11.2.40)

warnings.text: One who seeks blessings in return is a merchant, not a servant.

name: Singing the Lord's names (kīrtana, nāma-saṅkīrtana)
method_summary: Singing or reciting the names and deeds of the Lord, alone or together; declared the fearless way for all (BhP 2.1.11) and the means of the Kali age that gives what meditation, sacrifice and worship gave in earlier ages (BhP 12.3.51-52; VP 6.2.17).
signs_of_progress: love born, heart melted, laughing, weeping and dancing 'like one mad' (BhP 11.2.40)

warnings.text: The ten offences against the name (as cited from the Padma) obstruct its fruit.

name: Hearing the Purāṇa (kathā-śravaṇa)
method_summary: Listening with faith to the recitation and exposition of the Purāṇa by a qualified reciter, the first step of the Bhāgavata's path (hearing leads to taste, purification, steady devotion and knowledge of the Lord), with rules for giving and honouring the text.

name: The seven-day hearing of the Bhāgavata (saptāha)
method_summary: A formal recital of the whole Bhāgavata over seven days, modelled on Śuka's teaching to Parīkṣit, with vows for the hearers; the Māhātmya praises it above sacrifice, vows, yoga and meditation and tells how it freed the preta Dhundhukārī.

name: Recitation of the Devī Māhātmya (Caṇḍīpāṭha)
method_summary: Reciting the thirteen chapters of the Devī Māhātmya (with ancillary hymns in the recitation tradition), especially on the eighth, ninth and fourteenth lunar days and during the autumn Navarātra; the Goddess promises protection and prosperity to reciters and hearers (DM 12).

name: Repetition of the five-syllable mantra of Śiva
method_summary: Repetition of 'namaḥ śivāya' (with Oṃ, six syllables), received from the teacher, as the chief means of Śaiva worship and liberation.

name: Worship of the liṅga
method_summary: Worship of Śiva in the formless liṅga (including liṅgas made of earth for the occasion), with bathing, bilva leaves, lamps and offerings; the Śiva Purāṇa teaches that Śiva alone may be worshipped in the liṅga because he alone is niṣkala.

name: Meditation on the deity's form
method_summary: Holding the mind on the form of the Lord in the heart or before the mind's eye, limb by limb from the feet to the smiling face, until it does not waver; then simplifying the form (without weapons, without ornaments, one limb) or dwelling on the face (BhP 2.2.8-14; 3.28.12-33; VP 6.7.75-90).
stage: intermediate; after ethical preparation, posture and breath
signs_of_progress: the form stays in mind whether walking, standing or acting (VP 6.7.87)

name: Meditation in the heart-lotus (Uddhava's instruction)
method_summary: Seated evenly, gaze at the nose-tip, purify the breath-channels, raise Oṃ in the heart like a bell; visualise the upturned eight-petalled heart-lotus with sun, moon and fire in its pericarp and the Lord's form in the fire; meditate on all its limbs, then on the smile, then fix the mind in space, then think of nothing; the self is seen in the Lord, light in light (BhP 11.14.32-46).

warnings.text: Keep far from the company of the attached; meditate in a secluded, safe place.

name: Holding the mind on the auspicious support (VP 6.7)
method_summary: With breath and senses mastered, fix the mind on Viṣṇu's form as the ground of all powers, simplifying it stage by stage, until dhyāna (a single continuous flow) and samādhi (grasping the object's own nature free of imagination) arise.

name: Meditation on Oṃ (MkP 42)
method_summary: Repeat and contemplate the one syllable Oṃ: its three measures (a, u, m) and the half-measure beyond the guṇas felt at the crown; breath the bow, self the arrow, Brahman the target; become one with the imperishable.

name: The seven subtle dhāraṇās (MkP 40)
method_summary: Holding the mind at the head on earth, water, fire, air, space, mind and intellect in turn, experiencing and then abandoning the subtlety of each, without attachment to any.

warnings.text: Attachment to any element's subtlety destroys the yogin and he returns (to rebirth).

name: Śaiva meditation with and without object
method_summary: Meditation on Śiva's form (Śrīkaṇṭha) first, with an object and a seed, and at the end without object or seed, as awareness of the formless self; knowing the meditator, the act, the object and the purpose.

name: Purāṇic prāṇāyāma
method_summary: Breath-mastery in exhalation, inhalation and retention, neither hurried nor slow, after purifying the channels, practised gradually and often joined with mantra (with 'seed') or without; it burns faults and brings calm, the dispelling of darkness, inner light and clarity.
notes: Summary only: the texts' counts and grades of retention are not reproduced.

warnings.text: Practise neither fast nor slow, step by step.
Do not practise overfed, hungry, tired or in unsuitable places and times; faults such as deafness, dullness and fever follow.

name: Ritual worship of the deity (pūjā, arcana)
method_summary: Worship of the deity in an image, liṅga or yantra with offerings; one of the nine forms of devotion and the chief means of the Dvāpara age.

name: Vows (vrata)
method_summary: Observances for a lunar day or a period - fasting, vigil, worship, recitation and gifts - dedicated to a deity, with a story and a promised fruit.
notes: Prolonged fasts (e.g. month-long regimens) are restricted content and are not detailed here.

name: The Ekādaśī vow
method_summary: Fasting and worship of Viṣṇu on the eleventh lunar day of each fortnight, with vigil and breaking of the fast on the twelfth.

name: The Śivarātri vow
method_summary: Fast and night-long vigil with worship of the liṅga on Śiva's night; the hunter who kept it unknowingly was saved.

name: The Navarātra vow of the Goddess
method_summary: Nine nights of worship of the Goddess (especially in autumn), with recitation of the Devī Māhātmya and worship of young girls.

name: The Kātyāyanī vow of the gopīs
method_summary: A month-long observance in Mārgaśīrṣa by unmarried girls: early bathing in the river, worship of the goddess Kātyāyanī in an image of sand, and prayer to obtain the desired husband (for the gopīs, Kṛṣṇa).

name: Pilgrimage to tīrthas
method_summary: Journeying to holy places, bathing, worship, gifts and śrāddha there; seven cities give liberation; the inner meaning is purity of mind and the company of the holy, who themselves make places holy.

warnings.text: The greedy, cruel and hypocritical remain impure though they bathe in every tīrtha.

name: Bathing in the inner tīrtha
method_summary: Cultivating truth, forbearance, sense-control, compassion, straightforwardness, giving, self-restraint, contentment, celibacy, kind speech, knowledge, steadiness and austerity - 'bathing in the lake of knowledge that removes the dirt of passion and hatred'.

name: Giving (dāna) and the great gifts
method_summary: Religious gifts - food, water, land, cows, gold, sesame and the sixteen great gifts - to worthy recipients at due times and places; gifts in life ease the road after death.

name: Care of the dying (Purāṇic)
method_summary: Turning the dying person's mind to the Lord (remembrance, the name), gifts made by or for the dying (above all the Vaitaraṇī cow), and the recitation of sacred texts.
notes: Further customary acts (placing on the ground, sesame, Gaṅgā water, tulasī) are described in the Pretakalpa's later chapters; not checked verse by verse.

name: Remembering the Lord at death
method_summary: Directing the mind to the Lord (Nārāyaṇa, Kṛṣṇa, Śiva) at the time of death, prepared by lifelong remembrance, since the last thought shapes the next state; the name uttered at death protects (Ajāmila).

warnings.text: Attachment at death leads to an according birth (Bharata's deer).

name: Yogic departure at death
method_summary: The yogin, choosing the time of death, withdraws the mind, restrains the breaths and leaves the body through the crown, either for immediate liberation or for the gradual ascent (BhP 2.2.15-31). Summary only.

warnings.text: Addressed to the accomplished yati; the Vāyavīya asks how the practiser who dies before completing yoga avoids becoming a self-killer (ātmahā).

name: Fasting unto death (prāyopaveśa)
method_summary: The vow of sitting without food until death with the mind fixed on the Lord, as Parīkṣit did on the Gaṅgā after the curse. Recorded only as the text's narrative.
notes: Restricted (prolonged fasting): summary only. The Pretakalpa has a chapter on the destiny of those who die by fasting (2.36, title checked, content not read).

name: Offering piṇḍas for the dead
method_summary: Offering rice-balls with sesame and water to the dead for the first ten days (which build the preta's body), then monthly through the year.

name: Śrāddha
method_summary: Rites of faith for the dead and the ancestors - ekoddiṣṭa for the preta, the sixteen śrāddhas, monthly and annual rites, pārvaṇa for the three ancestors - with feeding of brahmins; they feed the dead on Yama's road and satisfy the ancestors.

name: Sapiṇḍīkaraṇa
method_summary: The rite that unites the preta's piṇḍa with those of father, grandfather and great-grandfather, ending the preta state; preferably on the twelfth day, or after three fortnights, six months or a year.

name: Release of a bull (vṛṣotsarga)
method_summary: On the eleventh day a consecrated bull is set free for the dead; without it the preta state becomes fixed.

name: Nārāyaṇa-bali
method_summary: An offering to Nārāyaṇa for one who died a bad or untimely death, allowing the regular rites to take effect.

name: The gift of the Vaitaraṇī cow
method_summary: Giving a (dark) cow to a brahmin at or before death so that the dead may cross the Vaitaraṇī by boat.

name: Śrāddha at Gayā
method_summary: Offering piṇḍas at Gayā's sacred spots in sequence for the release of the ancestors.

name: Śrāddha for oneself while living
method_summary: A śrāddha performed for oneself during life (by those without heirs or seeking release), taught in LiP 2.45 and the Pretakalpa (ch. 8, 'self-śrāddha').
notes: Chapter titles checked (LiP 2.45 'jīvacchrāddhavidhi'; GP 2.8 'śrāddhakartr-ātmaśrāddha'); contents not read; no teaching extracted yet.
